section.heading: Hyphenated Words
section.p: These are the potential solutions to a third party infringement claim.
Courts weigh third party status when a subpoena is challenged.
The agency sought documents from a third-party.
Records held by third-parties were excluded from the review.
The company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the parent.
The regulator reviewed publicly-owned companies and wholly-owned units.
The firm advised a closely-held company on a privately-funded project.
These questions are governed by common law principles of proximate causation.
Roman law informed the common-law of England in later centuries.
The agency adopted a risk based approach to enforcement.
The parties signed a long term supply contract.
A party to a litigation may obtain documents from third parties.
Courts consider third-party status in deciding whether a subpoena is unduly burdensome.
A third party's obligation to preserve evidence is far more limited than that of the parties.
The company is a wholly owned subsidiary, and the agency reviewed publicly owned companies.
These questions are governed by common-law principles, and the common law of England informed them.
The firm advised a closely held company on a publicly funded project.
The supply contract runs for a long time, and the approach is based on risk.
